source.title: Stabilizing Sharpness-aware Minimization Through A Simple Renormalization Strategy
source.authors: Cheng-Li Tan; Jiang-She Zhang; Jun-Min Liu; Yicheng Wang; Yunda Hao

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training–test loss gaps and parameter distance under different optimizers, using measures distinct from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on image classification and paired-model stability experiments. Its sharpness results compare Hessian eigenvalues across optimizers but do not pair them with generalization gaps, so they do not test V7's stated relationship. Figure-only gap values are not numerically recoverable from the text.
record.test_reason: The study develops SSAM using the premise that flatter minima generalize better and evaluates optimizer performance and stability. It does not test any listed version: SAM variants are not an Adam-versus-SGD comparison, and Hessian eigenvalues do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that renormalization stabilizes sharpness-aware training and that SSAM achieves comparable or sometimes better held-out accuracy than SAM. They report positive correspondence between parameter distance and the loss gap. Their theoretical comparisons concern bounds under strongly convex assumptions and learning-rate restrictions; tighter gap bounds alone do not guarantee better held-out performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares SAM and its renormalized variant with SGD, rather than applying the interventions or measurements in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported gap and parameter-distance trajectories vary with optimizer and dataset (MNIST FCN versus CIFAR-10 LeNet).

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that parameter distance between models trained on datasets differing by one example moves positively with the absolute training–test loss gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter sensitivity to replacing one training example tracks the generalization gap in the tested MNIST FCN and CIFAR-10 LeNet experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1 and 2 compare held-out accuracy of SGD or AdamW with SAM variants; SSAM usually matches or improves upon SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Renormalizing SAM's descent gradient can preserve or improve held-out image-classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 reports smaller leading Hessian eigenvalues for SAM than SGD and the smallest for SSAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSAM finds solutions with smaller leading Hessian eigenvalues in the tested ResNet settings.

record.problems: The paired-model gap results are presented as figures without numeric values in the text. The text describes positive correlation but supplies no correlation coefficient or statistical test.
record.rows_left_out: The optimizer test-accuracy comparisons in Tables 1 and 2 and Hessian eigenvalue comparisons in Figure 8 are not extracted: they compare performance or sharpness across optimizers without measuring a claim-version outcome or a paired sharpness–gap relationship. Other figure-only optimization results likewise do not measure the listed versions.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate.
No matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison; the FCN and LeNet use different datasets.
No matched adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison. ImageNet transformers use AdamW, while ResNets use SGD, with different architectures and training budgets.
No batch-size intervention under matched epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention; excluding dropout in the stability experiments does not test its effect.

No magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measure, comparison of its gap rankings with norm and margin measures, or matched low-training-loss analysis. Hessian eigenvalues and held-out accuracy do not establish the specified relationship.
Replacing one random example measures stability, not accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The optimizer-accuracy and Hessian results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out and do not warrant missing entries. Removing batch normalization before Hessian estimation does not turn the eigenvalue measure into V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison on the same image task.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the version's tuning conditions are not tested.
The study does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test its ranking against generalization gaps.
